content.title: About
content.content: Fruit cocktail in syrup is a mixture of diced fruits (typically pineapple, peach, pear, cherry and orange) preserved in a sweet sugar syrup. The product is produced by hot sterilization, giving it a long shelf‑life without refrigeration.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canned fruit cocktail is often used as a quick ingredient for desserts, salads and drinks.
The syrup usually contains about 20‑30 % sugar, which helps retain the bright colour and aroma of the fruits.
In the former Soviet Union a similar product was called “fruit mix in syrup” and was popular in school cafeterias.
Most manufacturers add a small amount of citric acid to stabilise flavour and prevent fruit darkening.
Fruit cocktail is frequently used as a base for homemade ice cream and fruit jellies.

items.title: Source of Vitamin C
items.content: The fruits retain some vitamin C, which supports the immune system and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Dietary Fiber
items.content: Fiber content aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports heart function.

items.title: Low Fat
items.content: The product contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The syrup provides additional liquid, useful during periods of increased fluid loss.

items.title: High Sugar Content
items.content: The syrup is high in sugar, so consumption should be moderate, especially for people with diabetes or those watching their weight.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Some brands use preservatives such as potassium sorbate, which may cause allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Bisphenol A in Cans
items.content: Long‑term storage in metal cans can lead to BPA migration; choosing BPA‑free or glass packaging is advisable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fruit cocktail can be eaten straight from the jar, added to yogurt, oatmeal, muesli, used as a filling for pancakes, pies and cakes, or blended into smoothies and cocktails. Draining part of the syrup is recommended for a less sweet version.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 3‑5 days. Discard if any off‑odor or colour change occurs.
